_comment: Differences the parity check should not fail on. Everything here is a
decision someone made, not a difference nobody got round to. If a line
cannot be justified in one sentence it does not belong in this file —
an allowlist that absorbs unexplained drift is how OP-227 survived for
_why_enabled_labels: The catalog labels a service's toggle after the service's own name, so it
reads 'Enable Elastic Kubernetes Service (EKS)' where the static config
says 'Enable EKS'. Both are correct; the catalog's is unambiguous in a list
of service cards, which is where the toggle is actually read. Accepted.
_why_empty_vs_null: The templates ship "" and {} for these; the static config claims null.
The catalog reports what Terraform will actually receive, so it is the
accurate side. Accepted rather than 'fixed' in the static config, which
_why_fields: EKS addon flags and the node-group AMI switch are real Terraform knobs the
static config never exposed. They appear on the EKS service card once the
wizard hydrates from the catalog — which is the point of OP-202: a knob
added to the templates reaches the wizard without a frontend release.
These are NOT Helm charts; those have their own wizard step and their own
config, and the catalog deliberately does not carry them (OP-200).
eks.ingressDomain is the customer's own domain, added by OP-244. The generated
output used to hardcode openprime.io — our domain — so the monitoring ingresses
resolved for nobody and the ArgoCD ALB never found a certificate. Catalog-only,
because the static config has no notion of a domain at all.
